whatItIs.text: A cool-climate cereal grass whose flattened seeds make porridge, granola, and flour; oats need less summer heat and more rain than wheat, so they ruled Northwest Europe.

historyNote.text: Oats were domesticated as a secondary crop — they simply arrived as weed-seeds among other cereals and were kept — while their wild ancestor grew in the Fertile Crescent; they thrive in poor acid soils other grains won't.

howToChoose.text: Choose rolled oats for baking and quick porridge, steel-cut for chew; check the date, since oats can go rancid like any whole grain.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry cupboard.

useItUp.text: Stale oats toast well into granola, blitz into oat flour for pancakes, or steep in milk overnight — porridge requires almost nothing else.

substitutions.note: for thickening and bakes; adds gluten, changes texture
